Where does your body's adrenaline come from?

Adrenaline is made by two tiny glands sitting on top of your kidneys, called the adrenal glands. When you're scared or surprised, they quickly release adrenaline into your blood!

Saan nanggagaling ang adrenaline sa katawan?

Ang adrenaline ay gawa ng dalawang maliit na glandula sa ibabaw ng iyong mga bato, tinatawag na adrenal glands. Kapag natakot o nagulat ka, agad nilang inilalabas ang adrenaline sa dugo mo!
copy.bis:
Asa naggikan ang adrenaline sa lawas?

Ang adrenaline gihimo sa duha ka gagmay nga glandula sa ibabaw sa imong mga kidney, gitawag og adrenal glands. Kon mahadlok o makalitan ka, dali dayon nilang ibuga ang adrenaline sa imong dugo!

copy.tl: Isipin mong biglang nagpreno ang jeepney na sinasakyan mo at muntik ka nang mabangga — kumakabog ang puso mo at parang nanlalamig ka. Iyon ang adrenaline na sumusugod sa katawan mo!
copy.bis: Hunahunaa nga kalit nga moprenó ang jeepney nga imong gisakyan ug hapit ka mabangga — mokusog ang pitik sa imong kasingkasing ug morag mobugnaw ka. Kana ang adrenaline nga mibuhagay sa imong lawas!

copy.en:
Why is constant stress unhealthy?

Adrenaline helps in short bursts, but constant stress means your body always has adrenaline — which tires you out and isn't good for the heart. Rest and calming down matter.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi maganda ang laging stress?

Nakakatulong ang adrenaline sa maikling sandali, pero kung laging stressed ka, laging may adrenaline ang katawan mo — nakakapagod ito at hindi maganda sa puso. Kaya mahalaga ang pahinga at pagpapakalma.
copy.bis:
Nganong dili maayo ang kanunay stress?

Makatabang ang adrenaline sa mubo nga panahon, apan kon kanunay kang stressed, kanunay adunay adrenaline ang imong lawas — makakapoy kini ug dili maayo sa kasingkasing. Mao nga importante ang pahulay ug pagpakalma.

Pinupuno ito ng compressed air! Maraming air particles sa loob ang tumutulak palabas sa goma. Kaya kaya nitong buhatin ang sasakyan at tumalbog ang bola!

Mas mabilis ba kumulo ang tubig sa tuktok ng mataas na bundok?

Oo! Sa mataas na bundok, mas mababa ang presyon ng hangin, kaya kumukulo ang tubig sa mas mababang temperatura.

Ang dagkong sungay o hayag nga kolor nagpakita kon unsa ka kusog o himsog ang usa ka hayop—busa usahay mosibog na lang ang kaaway nga dili na kinahanglan makig-away!

Aduna bay kidney ang mga mananap?

Oo! Ang baboy, iro, ug isda adunay usab kidney nga naghago sa paglimpyo sa ilang dugo.

Nope! Many think she bosses everyone like a king, but her only real job is laying eggs — worker ants do their tasks all on their own.
copy.tl:
Nag-uutos ba ang reyna ng mga langgam?

Hindi pala! Akala ng marami parang hari siya, pero mangitlog lang talaga ang trabaho niya — kusa namang gumagawa ng tungkulin ang mga manggagawang langgam.

Nagmando ba ang reyna sa mga hulmigas?

Dili diay! Daghan ang naghunahuna nga sama siya sa hari, pero ang bugtong buluhaton niya mao ang pangitlog — kusa ra magbuhat sa ilang trabaho ang mga trabahante nga hulmigas.

Ang arachnid ay hayop na may walong paa, dalawang bahagi ng katawan, at walang antena ni pakpak — gaya ng gagamba, scorpion, at garapata!

assignedReviews.reason: The card defines an atoll, a natural landform, but does not identify a local example nor describe how it influences non-living and living components, which are the core actions of the competency.

copy.en: An atoll is a beautiful, ring-shaped reef that forms a circle around a calm, central lagoon!
copy.tl: Ang atoll ay isang magandang reef na hugis-singsing, na gumagawa ng bilog sa paligid ng isang lagoon sa gitna!
copy.bis: Ang atoll usa ka nindot nga reef nga porma og singsing, nga naghimo og bilog sa palibot sa lagoon sa tunga!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is the most accurate clock ever!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the accuracy of an atomic clock, which is a science invention, but it does not use information from the home or local community, nor does it explain the invention's impact on everyday life. It only states a fact about accuracy, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Just how accurate is the atomic clock compared to all other clocks?

It is the most accurate clock ever! It may lose only one second over millions of years.
copy.tl:
Gaano katumpak ang atomic clock kumpara sa ibang mga orasan?

Ito ang pinakatumpak na orasan! Maaari lang itong mawalan ng isang segundo sa loob ng milyun-milyong taon.
copy.bis:
Unsa katukma ang atomic clock kumpara sa ubang mga relo?

Kini ang labing tukmang relo! Mawad-an lang kini og usa ka segundo sa minilyon ka tuig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists need a super powerful tool called an electron microscope to actually take pictures of atoms!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that scientists use models to explain phenomena that cannot be easily seen or detected
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses using an electron microscope to see atoms, not using models to explain phenomena that cannot be easily seen. It does not mention models or how models help explain unseen phenomena, so it only shares the general idea that atoms are too small for ordinary microscopes.

copy.en:
Can we see atoms using our school microscope?

Nope! Ordinary microscopes aren't strong enough. Scientists need a super powerful tool called an electron microscope to actually take pictures of atoms!
copy.tl:
Makikita ba natin ang atomo gamit ang school microscope?

Hindi! Hindi sapat ang ordinaryong mikroskopyo. Kailangan ng scientists ng napakalakas na electron microscope para makakuha ng larawan ng mga atomo!
copy.bis:
Makita ba nato ang atomo gamit ang school microscope?

Dili! Dili igo ang ordinaryong mikroskopyo. Kinahanglan sa mga scientist og kusgan kaayo nga electron microscope para makakuha og hulagway sa mga atomo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Auroras appear near the magnetic poles!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses auroras, a sky phenomenon, but the competency specifically targets observing and describing the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars. Auroras are not among the listed celestial objects and the card does not support observing or describing those objects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth's magnetic field acts like a guide, leading particles from the Sun toward the far north and far south.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions solar particles and Earth's magnetic field but does not describe electromagnetic radiation as energy created by vibrating charged particles or as transverse waves. It does not directly support the competency's core concept of EMR.

copy.en: Auroras appear near the magnetic poles! Earth's magnetic field acts like a guide, leading particles from the Sun toward the far north and far south.
copy.tl: Lumalabas ang aurora malapit sa magnetic poles! Ang magnetic field ng Earth ang gumagabay sa mga particle mula sa araw papunta sa malalayong hilaga at timog.
copy.bis: Mogawas ang aurora duol sa magnetic poles! Ang magnetic field sa Yuta ang naggiya sa mga partikulo gikan sa adlaw padulong sa layo nga amihanan ug habagatan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If a trip is 240 kilometers and the bus averages 60 km/h, it takes about 4 hours to get there.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card applies the speed formula (distance ÷ speed = time) but never states or identifies that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. It assumes the concept rather than teaching the definition, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How do you know when you'll arrive?

Use average speed! If a trip is 240 kilometers and the bus averages 60 km/h, it takes about 4 hours to get there.
copy.tl:
Paano mo malalaman kung kailan ka darating?

Gamitin ang average speed! Kung 240 kilometro ang biyahe at ang bus ay 60 km/h ang average, aabutin ka ng mga 4 na oras.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nimo pagkahibalo kung kanus-a ka moabot?

Gamita ang average speed! Kung 240 kilometros ang biyahe ug ang bus 60 km/h ang average, mokabat kini og mga 4 ka oras.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A baby is born with about 300 bones—more than an adult—which fuse together as the baby grows.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a factual trivia point about the number of bones in a baby and their fusion, but it does not describe how the skeletal system works (e.g., support, movement, protection). It shares the skeletal-system topic but gives no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
How many bones does a baby have?

A baby is born with about 300 bones—more than an adult—which fuse together as the baby grows.
copy.tl:
Ilang buto ang taglay ng sanggol?

Isinisilang ang sanggol na may halos 300 na buto, na unti-unting nagsasama-sama habang siya'y lumalaki.
copy.bis:
Pila ka bukog ang masuso?

Ang masuso natawo nga adunay mga 300 ka bukog, nga magtapok samtang kini nagdako.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a baby can already move and kick
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the female reproductive system as ovaries, uterus, and vagina and those of the male reproductive system as the prostate, testis, and penis and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions fetal movement before birth but does not identify or describe the parts of the female or male reproductive system or how they work. It is only loosely related to pregnancy/reproduction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a baby can already move and kick
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions movement and kicking, which could involve the muscular system, but it does not describe the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems or how they work. It provides no direct instructional support for this competency.

copy.en: Even before birth, a baby can already move and kick—and mom can sometimes feel it!
copy.tl: Bago pa ipanganak, kaya na palang gumalaw at sumipa ng sanggol—at minsan nararamdaman ito ng ina!
copy.bis: Sa wala pa matawo, ang bata makahimo na og lihok ug sipa—ug usahay mabati kini sa inahan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it drinks milk from its mother
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a baby sheep drinking milk, which is a mammalian trait, but it does not state that sheep give birth to live young or contrast live birth with egg-laying. It does not directly support identifying reproductive groups.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A baby sheep is called a lamb
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a baby sheep as a lamb but does not classify sheep into any named group (e.g., mammal) or use a table. It does not support the classification competency.

copy.en: A baby sheep is called a lamb, and just like human babies, it drinks milk from its mother.
copy.tl: Ang anak ng tupa ay tinatawag na lamb o kordero, at tulad ng ibang sanggol, sumususo rin ito ng gatas sa kanyang ina.
copy.bis: Ang nati sa karnero gitawag og lamb o kordero, ug sama sa ubang bata, mosuso usab kini og gatas sa iyang inahan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is a bacterium
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card names a bacterium but does not state that bacteria are unicellular or contrast them with multicellular organisms. It provides no direct instruction on the single-cell vs. many-cell concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: kills insects but is harmless to humans, animals, and the environment
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a bacterium harming insects and not harming others, but it does not explain the interaction between living things or between living and non-living things bringing good or harm. It is a factual statement about a biopesticide, not an explanation of ecological interactions.

copy.en: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is a bacterium that makes a natural toxin that kills insects but is harmless to humans, animals, and the environment — farmers use it as a safe biopesticide.
copy.tl: Ang Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) ay bakteryang gumagawa ng natural na lason na pumapatay ng insekto pero hindi nakasasama sa tao, hayop, o kalikasan — ginagamit ito bilang ligtas na biopesticide.
copy.bis: Ang Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) usa ka bakterya nga naghimo og natural nga lason nga nagpatay sa insekto apan dili makadaot sa tawo, mananap, o kalikasan — gigamit kini isip luwas nga biopesticide.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bad smell, weird color, slimy texture, or fuzzy growth all mean bacteria have spoiled your food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things in the environment, such as trash disposal, and burning household materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes signs of food spoilage caused by bacteria, which is a change in a material (food) that can be harmful to humans. However, G3-M-6 focuses on changes in materials that are harmful to living and non-living things in the environment, with examples like trash disposal and burning household materials. Food spoilage is not an environmental harm example and does not directly teach the competency's intended concept of environmental harm from material changes.

copy.en: Bad smell, weird color, slimy texture, or fuzzy growth all mean bacteria have spoiled your food — never eat it if you see these signs!
copy.tl: Masamang amoy, pagbabago ng kulay, malagkit na texture, o may lumalaking bagay — lahat ito ay senyales na sinira na ng bacteria ang pagkain, kaya huwag itong kainin!
copy.bis: Masamang amoy, pagbag-o sa kolor, mapilit nga texture, o adunay nagtubo — kining tanan mga senyales nga nadaot na sa bakterya ang pagkaon, ayaw gyud kaona!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bacteria are among the very first living things that appeared on Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bacteria but does not address unicellular vs multicellular organisms, single cells, or humans. It provides no instructional support for recognizing that some organisms consist of a single cell and others of many cells.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bacteria are among the very first living things that appeared on Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the geologic time scale helps to recount the history of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about early life on Earth but does not explain the geologic time scale or how it helps recount Earth's history. It shares the broad topic of Earth's history but gives no direct support for the competency.

copy.en:
What was among Earth's first life?

Bacteria are among the very first living things that appeared on Earth, billions and billions of years ago!
copy.tl:
Ano ang isa sa pinakaunang buhay sa Daigdig?

Ang bakterya ay kabilang sa pinakaunang nabubuhay na lumitaw sa Daigdig, bilyon-bilyong taon na ang nakalipas!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang usa sa pinakaunang buhi sa Kalibotan?

Ang bakterya kauban sa pinakauna nga buhing butang nga mitungha sa Kalibotan, bilyon-bilyon ka tuig na ang milabay!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Millions of helpful bacteria live inside your intestines!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions intestines but does not identify or describe the parts of the digestive system (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) or how they work. It focuses on gut bacteria, not the digestive system anatomy or function required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Millions of helpful bacteria live inside your intestines!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using a labeled diagram, trace how food travels through the digestive tract and explain how different digestive processes work, including mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, and elimination
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a labeled diagram to trace food through the digestive tract nor explain digestive processes (mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, elimination). It only states that bacteria in the intestines help break down food and make vitamins, which is tangential to the competency's required content and format.

copy.en: Millions of helpful bacteria live inside your intestines! They break down food your body can't on its own, and even make some vitamins for you.
copy.tl: Milyon-milyong mabubuting bacteria ang naninirahan sa loob ng iyong bituka! Tinutulungan ka nilang masira ang pagkaing hindi kaya ng sarili mong katawan, at gumagawa pa sila ng ilang bitamina para sa iyo.
copy.bis: Minilyon nga maayong bacteria ang nagpuyo sa sulod sa imong tinai! Gitabangan ka nila sa pagdugmok sa pagkaon nga dili kaya sa imong lawas, ug naghimo pa sila og pipila ka bitamina para nimo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bagoong is made from tiny fish or shrimp packed with plenty of salt so it keeps for a long time!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions salt as a preservative for bagoong, which touches on food preservation, but it does not explain any factor affecting the rates of chemical reactions (e.g., temperature, concentration, surface area) or the underlying mechanism. It only states a fact about how bagoong is made, providing no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
How is bagoong made to keep for a long time?

Bagoong is made from tiny fish or shrimp packed with plenty of salt so it keeps for a long time!
copy.tl:
Paano ginagawa ang bagoong para tumagal nang matagal?

Ang bagoong ay gawa sa maliliit na isda o alamang na binudburan ng maraming asin upang tumagal nang matagal!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimo sa ginamos (bagoong) aron molungtad og dugay?

Ang ginamos (bagoong) hinimo gikan sa gagmay nga isda o alamang nga gisagolan og daghang asin aron molungtad og dugay!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The scientific name of baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3).
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a name and formula for one compound. It does not describe properties of pure substances, fixed chemical composition, elements vs compounds, or the unique proton number of an element's atoms. The content is only tangentially related to compounds.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The scientific name of baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3).
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: write the chemical formula and chemical names of some common ionic compounds, including sodium chloride (NaCl), magnesium oxide (MgO), potassium chloride (KCl) and magnesium chloride (MgCl2)
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives the name and formula of one ionic compound, but the competency requires writing chemical formulas and names of several common ionic compounds (NaCl, MgO, KCl, MgCl2). The card does not teach the skill of writing formulas/names or cover the listed examples; it merely presents a single fact.

copy.en: The scientific name of baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3). Science in your kitchen!
copy.tl: Ang siyentipikong pangalan ng baking soda ay sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3). Siyensya sa kusina mo!
copy.bis: Ang siyentipikong ngalan sa baking soda kay sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3). Siyensya sa imong kusina!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Activities like dancing and playing help improve our balance and coordination.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions balance and coordination, which relate to the muscular and skeletal systems, but it does not describe how any body system works. It only states that activities improve balance and coordination, providing no instructional support for the competency's requirement to describe the functioning of the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems.

copy.en: Activities like dancing and playing help improve our balance and coordination.
copy.tl: Ang mga aktibidad tulad ng pagsayaw at paglalaro ay nagpapabuti sa ating balanse at koordinasyon.
copy.bis: Ang mga kalihokan sama sa pagsayaw ug pagdula makapauswag sa atong balanse ug koordinasyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Being full and eating balanced are not the same thing!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses balanced eating and nutrient variety, not identifying basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It only tangentially relates to food as a need.

copy.en: Being full and eating balanced are not the same thing! You could fill up on rice alone and still be missing veggies, fruit, and protein.
copy.tl: Iba ang busog sa balanse! Puwede kang mabusog sa kanin lang pero kulang pa rin sa gulay, prutas, at protina.
copy.bis: Lahi ang pagkabusog sa balanse! Mahimong mabusog ka sa kan-on lang apan kulang gihapon sa utanon, prutas, ug protina.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a big balete has so many root-pillars
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions roots (root-pillars) but does not describe their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil. It only notes that many root-pillars make the tree look like a small forest, which does not directly support the competency's focus on root function.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a big balete has so many root-pillars
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to root-pillars (aerial roots) but does not describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants. It only states that the many root-pillars make the tree look like a forest, without explaining their function or purpose as required by the competency.

copy.en:
Can one tree look like a whole forest?

Yes — a big balete has so many root-pillars that it can look like a small forest, even though it's just one tree!
copy.tl:
Puwede bang magmukhang gubat ang isang puno?

Oo — dahil sa dami ng haligi nitong ugat, ang malaking balete ay maaaring magmukhang maliit na gubat kahit isang puno lang ito!
copy.bis:
Mahimo bang morag lasang ang usa lang ka kahoy?

Oo — tungod sa daghan niining haligi nga gamot, ang dakong balete mahimong morag gamay nga lasang bisan usa ra kini ka kahoy!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: lives only in Palawan, Philippines
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a Philippine animal but does not use a drawing or diagram to classify it by habitat (terrestrial/aquatic/aerial). It only states the pangolin's geographic range, not its habitat category.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: lives only in Palawan, Philippines
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not make a list or table of animals and plants in a named habitat. It only gives a single fact about the pangolin's endemic location, not a habitat inventory.

copy.en: The balintong, or Philippine pangolin, lives only in Palawan, Philippines — nowhere else on Earth!
copy.tl: Ang balintong o Philippine pangolin ay matatagpuan lamang sa Palawan, Pilipinas — wala nang ibang lugar sa mundo!
copy.bis: Ang balintong o Philippine pangolin makit-an lamang sa Palawan, Pilipinas — wala nay laing lugar sa kalibutan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Air collects inside and pushes the rubber outward in every direction
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes air pressure inside a balloon, not the shape and volume properties of gases (no definite shape or volume). It does not directly support describing gas properties in terms of shape and volume.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Air collects inside and pushes the rubber outward in every direction
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies air occupies space inside the balloon, but it does not explicitly describe matter as having mass and taking up space. The focus is on air pressure, not the definition of matter.

copy.en:
Why does a balloon grow big and round when you blow it up?

Air collects inside and pushes the rubber outward in every direction, making the balloon firm and round!
copy.tl:
Bakit lumalaki at lumiloki ang lobo kapag hinipan mo?

Naiipon ang hangin sa loob at itinutulak nito ang goma palabas sa lahat ng direksyon, kaya tumitigas at lumoloki ang lobo!
copy.bis:
Nganong modako ug molingki ang balloon kon huypan nimo?

Motipon ang hangin sa sulod ug iduso niini ang goma pagawas sa tanang direksyon, mao nga motig-a ug molingki ang balloon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Balut is a duck egg with a partly grown baby duckling inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that balut is a duck egg containing a partly grown duckling. It does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants, nor does it describe stages from egg to mature organism. It merely references an early developmental stage of a bird, which is tangential to the competency's comparative focus.

copy.en:
What's really inside a balut?

Balut is a duck egg with a partly grown baby duckling inside — a popular food in the Philippines.
copy.tl:
Ano talaga ang laman ng balut?

Ang balut ay itlog ng bibe na may bahagyang lumaking sisiw sa loob — isang sikat na pagkain sa Pilipinas.
copy.bis:
Unsa gyud ang sulod sa balut?

Ang balut usa ka itlog sa bibe nga adunay gamayng nadako nga piso sa sulod — usa ka sikat nga pagkaon sa Pilipinas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bamboo is not a tree — it belongs to the grass family, making it a relative of rice and corn!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that bamboo belongs to the grass family, which touches on plant classification, but it does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups (flowering/non-flowering plants, animal groups, microorganisms). The format-required table is absent, and the content does not directly support the skill of classifying living things based on similar characteristics.

copy.en:
Is bamboo actually a tree?

Bamboo is not a tree — it belongs to the grass family, making it a relative of rice and corn!
copy.tl:
Puno ba talaga ang kawayan?

Hindi puno ang kawayan — kabilang ito sa pamilya ng damo, kaya kamag-anak ito ng palay at mais!
copy.bis:
Kahoy ba gyud ang kawayan?

Dili kahoy ang kawayan — sakop kini sa pamilya sa mga sagbot, busa paryente kini sa humay ug mais!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The banaba is a native Philippine tree known for its beautiful purple flowers
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the banaba tree and its leaves, but does not describe the outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) or their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil. The focus is on the tree's flowers and the medicinal use of its leaves, which is unrelated to the competency's specific instructional goal.

copy.en: The banaba is a native Philippine tree known for its beautiful purple flowers — and for ages, its leaves have been brewed into a medicinal tea.
copy.tl: Ang banaba ay katutubong punong Pilipino na kilala sa magagandang lilang bulaklak — at matagal nang ginagawang panlunas na tsaa ang mga dahon nito.
copy.bis: Ang banaba usa ka lumad nga kahoy sa Pilipinas nga inila sa nindot nga lila nga bulak — ug dugay na ning gigamit isip tambal nga tsa ang mga dahon niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: bananas are full of carbohydrates (starch) that give your body energy!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a specific food (saba banana) and its starch content providing energy. It does not teach that food is a basic need of living things, nor does it identify air, water, or shelter. The connection to 'food' as a basic need is only thematic, not instructional.

copy.en: Maruya is fried saba banana — and bananas are full of carbohydrates (starch) that give your body energy!
copy.tl: Ang maruya ay piniritong saging na saba — at ang saging ay puno ng karbohidrato (almirol) na nagbibigay ng enerhiya sa katawan!
copy.bis: Ang maruya mao ang giprito nga saging nga saba — ug ang saging puno sa karbohidrato (almirol) nga naghatag og kusog sa lawas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A banana's thick peel wraps around and protects the soft fruit inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a banana peel protecting the fruit, but the competency targets specialized plant structures such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots. A banana peel is not one of these specialized structures, and the card does not teach the purpose of the listed structures. It only shares the general idea of a protective plant part, which is related but not direct support.

copy.en: A banana's thick peel wraps around and protects the soft fruit inside—that's why we peel it off before eating!
copy.tl: May makapal na balat ang saging na bumabalot at nagpoprotekta sa malambot na laman sa loob—kaya tinatanggal natin ito bago kainin!
